title: presubmit-sculptor: split lint into stage-aware plugins and add release quiet-window hook
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Introduce presubmit-sculptor to reduce presubmit footprint; split lint into stage-aware plugin adapters; add release quiet-window hook to avoid noisy merges during major releases.
description:
Context and motivation: our presubmit pipeline has grown heavy and expensive for incremental changes. Teams repeatedly hit long lint and integration stages for small edits, which increases feedback time and developer context switches. This PR introduces a small presubmit orchestrator (presubmit-sculptor) plus a staged lint plugin architecture so we can target fast, language-aware lint passes in the fast lane and push heavier checks to gated stages or nightly runs. It also introduces a release quiet-window hook that temporarily suppresses non-blocking noisy checks during coordinated release merges.

Summary of changes (single-line commit summaries):
- feat(presubmit): add presubmit-sculptor command and config loader
- refactor(lint): split linter runners into stage-aware plugins (fast|full|nightly)
- ci: update .github/presubmit.yml to wire sculptor and stage selection
- ops: add release-quiesce hook and smallship script to scripts/release-quiesce.sh
- docs: document new presubmit config and onboarding flow in docs/dev/presubmit.md
- chore: bump eslint-plugin-compat and go-ci-runner deps for plugin interface compatibility

Files changed (high-level):
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (rewired lanes; added new fast-stage)
- tools/presubmit/sculptor.go (new orchestrator binary; config parsing, delta detection)
- tools/lint/plugins/fast_js.go (fast JS lint adapter)
- tools/lint/plugins/full_js.go (full JS lint adapter with type-aware checks)
- scripts/release-quiesce.sh (new helper for release windows)
- docs/dev/presubmit.md (developer-facing docs)
- ci/smoke-nightly.yaml (moved heavy checks to nightly lane)
- package.json (devdep bumps)
- Makefile (targets for presubmit/run-local)

Why this approach: sculptor runs a lightweight change detector to determine which files are in scope and maps them to a minimal set of lint plugins. For small edits (docs, README, small refactors) only fast-stage plugins run, providing sub-30s feedback for most changes. Larger changes trigger full-stage or the nightly lane where heavier SAST and slow linters run. The release quiet-window is an operational guard that mutes non-blocking noise (e.g., flakey flake-checkers) during release merges and surfaces only critical blockers.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implemented orchestrator and plugin interface
- [x] Wire presubmit workflow for fast/full/nightly lanes
- [x] Bumped minimal devdeps to match plugin interfaces
- [x] Added docs and local run targets
- [x] Added unit tests for sculptor (delta detection) and plugin loader
- [x] Manual dogfood run on core repo (observed ~40% presubmit time reduction on small PRs)

Testing/CI: initial CI runs failed due to a lint plugin interface mismatch (see conversation below). After bumping go-ci-runner to 0.18.1 and eslint-plugin-compat to 2.4.0, CI stabilized. Final merge CI status: all checks passed (unit tests, lint-fast, smoke-nightly scheduled for post-merge). We intentionally left the heavy nightly lane as optional in presubmit to avoid blocking merges.

Review conversation (condensed):
- Jensen Park (reviewer): "Nice direction — can we ensure the sculptor has a conservative fallback (run full-stage) if detection fails? Also request a small doc on how teams can opt-in for their own custom plugins."
- Author (Maya): "Added a conservative fallback in sculptor.go: if unknown extension mapping or plugin load error, we run full-stage and emit a telemetry event. Added docs section 'Extending plugins' in docs/dev/presubmit.md."
- Riya Kapoor: "Can we gate the release-quiesce by repo-level flag? We don't want cross-repo side effects during multi-repo releases."
- Author: "Added an opt-in flag 'release_quiet_allowed' in .github/presubmitrc; default false. scripts/release-quiesce.sh respects that flag per-repo."
- Liam O'Connor: "Suggest adding a metric for presubmit time saved so we can quantify wins."
- Author: "Added a basic telemetry ping (presubmit.duration_ms and presubmit.stage) to the sculptor; will wire to CI telemetry collector in a follow-up to keep this PR focused."

Edge cases and follow-ups:
- follow-up: ENG-3560 to add cross-repo release orchestration and central toggle for quiet-window
- follow-up: ENG-3573 to add telemetry ingestion and dashboard for presubmit time savings
- noted compatibility: some older devcontainers still have older node versions; docs include a 'devcontainer upgrade' section and Makefile has a shim target.

Merge outcome and method: Squash and merge. Merge commit message: "presubmit(sculptor): stage-aware lint plugins + release quiet-window". Post-merge actions: created a small canary rollout by enabling fast-stage for three teams and scheduled a smoke-nightly for the heavy lane. Observed metrics: median presubmit latency for small changes dropped from ~78s to ~44s in the canary set.

Why this PR is different from prior work: previous CI trimming PRs focused on CI matrix compression or cache keying. This change introduces a runtime presubmit decision layer and extensible plugin surface to adapt lint weight to change size and type. The addition of a scoped release quiet-window is intentionally operational (opt-in) and does not globally mute critical checks.
notes: Canary rollout started; further telemetry follow-ups planned.
